source.work: Supabase documentation, storage buckets and access control
source.paraphrase: Uploads belong in private buckets served through signed URLs or download policies. A bucket literally named public serves whatever lands in it.

invariants.why: Writing user uploads into a public bucket publishes them to anyone with the URL, including files the user thought were private.
invariants.fixHint: Upload into a named private bucket such as avatars, then serve reads through signed URLs or storage policies.
invariants.avoid: Quoting the name with backticks is still the public bucket. Reading from public with download is fine; writing is the flagged shape.

source.paraphrase: An rpc call names a Postgres function with a static string so generated types can check it. A zero-argument function is still rpc("name"). A name computed at runtime is not.

invariants.why: Generated Database types check a static function name, including a function whose Args are an empty record. A computed name skips that check, so the call can name a function the schema does not have.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the static function name from the generated types. Add the params object only when the function has arguments.
invariants.avoid: The rule runs only in a file that imports @supabase/supabase-js or @supabase/ssr. A static string or a static template with no substitution is allowed, with or without a params object. An interpolated or computed name stays untyped. A client that is not Supabase is not this call.

source.paraphrase: Subscriptions scope events with an .on() handler naming event, schema, and table. A bare channel streams everything it can see.

invariants.why: An unfiltered subscription pushes every change the key can read to the browser, multiplying realtime traffic and leaking rows the UI never shows.
invariants.fixHint: Add .on() with the event, schema, and table before .subscribe(), or use presence/broadcast with their own handlers.
invariants.avoid: Interpolating an id into the channel name is not a filter. Presence .on() handlers count as filters and are not flagged.

source.paraphrase: Clients invoke edge functions through supabase.functions.invoke, which attaches auth headers. A raw fetch to functions/v1 skips that handling.

invariants.why: A hand-rolled fetch must rebuild auth header forwarding, so tokens drift, refresh, and leak through manual plumbing instead of the client's handling.
invariants.fixHint: Call supabase.functions.invoke(name, { body }) and let the client attach the session.
invariants.avoid: A hand-set Authorization header is still manual plumbing. Plain fetch to the app's own routes is unaffected and is not flagged.
